findings.title: Unindexed `[~]` fixture example lacks the `**` bold-wrap the unindexed regex requires
findings.description: Task 1's example unindexed line is `7. [~] Feature Epsilon without explicit index — cut for scope.` — but `PLAN_UNINDEXED_RE` (`packages/core/src/introspection/parsers/slicePlanParser.ts:9`) is `/^(\d+)\.\s+\[([ xX])\]\s+\*\*([^(].*?)\*\*\s*(.*)/`, which requires `**Name**` bold-wrap. Every real unindexed entry (e.g. `packages/core/tests/fixtures/introspection/unindexed-slice-plan.md:12`) is bold-wrapped. An executor who transcribes the example verbatim gets a line that still matches neither regex and is still silently dropped, so Task 5's assertion that "the unindexed `[~]` entry parses with `status: 'deprecated'`... `indexSource: 'fallback'`" cannot pass. Task 1's success text only mandates the bold-wrap "for the indexed form," which invites exactly this failure. The example should be written as `7. [~] **Feature Epsilon** — cut for scope.` and the success text should require bold-wrap for both forms.

findings.title: Task 5 does not update the pre-existing assertions its fixture edit breaks outside `slicePlanParser.test.ts`
findings.description:
Task 1 adds two entries to `sample-slice-plan.md`, but Task 5's only "update existing test" instruction targets the `totalSlices`/`completedSlices` test (the design's `slicePlanParser.test.ts:44`). At least three other existing assertions against that fixture break and are named in no task:

- `packages/core/tests/introspection/slicePlanParser.test.ts:10` — `expect(result.entries).toHaveLength(5)` becomes 7.
- `packages/core/tests/introspection/slicePlanParser.test.ts:128` — `it('tags every entry indexSource: explicit...')` asserts `every((e) => e.indexSource === 'explicit')` on this fixture; adding an **unindexed** `[~]` line to `sample-slice-plan.md` makes `.every()` false, directly contradicting Task 1's requirement to put the unindexed line in this file.
- `packages/core/tests/introspection/ArtifactIntrospector.test.ts:52` — `expect(result.totalSlices).toBe(5)`.

Task 13's full-suite run would surface these only after the fact, which weakens Task 5's stated success criterion (`pnpm --filter @context-forge/core test -- slicePlanParser` passes — it wouldn't, and the ArtifactIntrospector failure is in a file Task 5 never mentions). Either update these assertions in Task 5's scope, or move the unindexed `[~]` line to `unindexed-slice-plan.md` (which resolves the `indexSource: 'explicit'` conflict and matches how the unindexed format is already fixture-tested).

findings.title: Success criterion naming `arch-status-vs-plans` has no covering test task
findings.description: Slice-design success criterion 6 reads "`ConsistencyChecker`'s `plan-status-vs-entries` / `arch-status-vs-plans` rules do not false-positive." Task 12 tests only `plan-status-vs-entries`. The sibling rule computes the same `allComplete` from `completedSlices`/`totalSlices` at `packages/core/src/introspection/ConsistencyChecker.ts:828-834` and flags against the **architecture** frontmatter status — a distinct input (`archStatus`) that the plan-status test never exercises. Task 12's complementary "in-progress still fires" case likewise only proves one direction of one rule. Add an `arch-status-vs-plans` case (arch frontmatter `status: complete`, plan entries all `[x]`/`[~]` → no finding) to Task 12, or state in the task why the arch rule is excluded.

findings.title: `Commit` markers are checklist items, not plain lines
findings.description: All six markers are written as `- [ ] Commit: ...` rather than plain `**Commit**:` lines. Placement is correct (after tested groups at tasks 5, 7, 10, 11, 12, plus a conditional one at 13 — not after every task, not only at the end), and this formatting appears to follow the CLAUDE.md rule requiring `[ ]` checkboxes on every subitem, so no action is required unless the plain-line convention takes precedence.

findings.title: Task 9's `derivedStatus` initializer change goes beyond the design's stated "one-line addition"
findings.description: Slice-design Decision 4 scopes `cf list slices` to "the same one-line addition to its inline `deriveEntryStatus({...})` call." Task 9 additionally rewrites the pre-try initializer at `packages/cli/src/commands/slice.ts:91`. The change is well-justified in the task text (prevents a filesystem error from reporting a `[~]` entry as `not-started`, consistent with CLAUDE.md's no-silent-fallback rule) and is small, but it is implementation instruction the design does not require — worth a one-line design addendum or acceptance as intentional.

findings.title: Task 10 asserts JSON output only; the `⊘ deprecated` table render is left to the manual walkthrough
findings.description: Success criterion 4 says `cf list slices` "renders the entry with the existing `⊘ deprecated` display." Task 10 asserts `status: 'deprecated'` and `isNext: false` in `--json` output; the table-rendering path (`renderEntryStatus` at `packages/cli/src/commands/slice.ts:178`) is exercised only by walkthrough step 3 in Task 13. Acceptable since `renderEntryStatus`'s `STATUS.Deprecated` case already exists and the JSON path proves `derivedStatus` is correct, but a table-form assertion would close it automatically.
